name: Moon Carver
desc: An Adeptus who lives on Qingyun Peak, Liyue.

customize.text: Moon Carver

Moon Carver is one of the Adepti of the south — illuminated beasts who received their title from the Prime of Adepti, Morax. Moon Carver is known for being the kindest Adeptus among all. He was the disciple of Rex Lapis and witnessed the Guili Assembly foundation. When the flood occurred, Moon Carver was one of the Adepti who helped people with the relocation. Together with Cloud Retainer, Marchosius, Mountain Shaper, and other Adepti, he protected people during the twelve-day storm that attacked them at the relocation. After the Archon War ended 3,700 years ago, the Liyue Harbor was founded, and the Adepti of the south swore to protect it.

After defeating all the gods in Liyue during the Archon War,
ascended to the divine throne and received the Geo Gnosis, becoming the Geo Archon. Together with the Adepti, he ruled the country of contracts, and soon Liyue became a major trading nation. 3,700 years after the beginning of his reign, Morax decided to pass the rule of Liyue to the Adepti and the people, leaving the post of an Archon. He played out his death in front of the people of the region and entered into "a contract to end all contracts" with the Cryo Archon. In his performance, Morax orchestrated the death of Geo Archon during one of the Rites of Descension. Upon learning of the incident, the Adepti were furious, believing that the Qixing, Liyue's rulers, had failed in their task and allowed the Archon's death. Moon Carver was the first one to greet the guests. He immediately said that he was aware of Travelers' unfair accusation and declared that he had an image of the real murderer. He decided to consult with the rest of Adepti to confirm his intuition.

While Liyue lay unprotected, the Eleventh Fatui Harbinger, Tartaglia, decided to provoke the Lord of Geo. Childe didn't believe in the Geo Archon's demise and resurrected one of the gods who perished during the Archon War, the Overlord of the Vortex, Osial, to force Rex Lapis to come to the defense of his people. This was how the Harbinger intended to obtain the Geo Gnosis. When Osial was awakened and began to threaten Liyue, Adepti, including Mountain Shaper, united with the Liyue Qixing to protect the harbor. Together, they defeated Osial and sent him back beneath the Guyun Stone Forest. After Rex Lapis appeared to the Adepti in a dream and told them of his plan, they agreed to entrust Qixing with the management of Liyue.

Liyue has its own fortune-telling, destiny-reading methods, similar to astrology. There are two fates that people seek to avoid at all costs: the "solitary star" and the "disastrous evil." The first fate dictates that one will be separated from friends and family, living alone all one's days. The second means that one will face many hardships and perils. One day, Moon Carver read the fate of the Cloud Retainer's disciple, Shenhe, and she was marked by these unfortunate fates. She was also plagued by intense homicidal urges, doomed to harm both herself and others. When the girl was five years old, her mother died of illness, and her father, unable to bear the pain of loss, became obsessed. One day, he set out to find a way to resurrect his wife and discovered the secret magical art of "Fate Transference": by making a ritual sacrifice to the seelie summoned by this art, a living person's body could be exchanged for a dead one's life. Returning after a year of searching, he decided to sacrifice his daughter. Shenhe's father took the girl to a cave and summoned a ferocious black "seelie," whose blood-red eyes craved Shenhe's life. The girl was stupefied, but she wanted to live. Gripping an exorcist's dagger, she fought the demon for several days until Cloud Retainer discovered her. When the Adepti learned of the girl's fate, which only appears once every thousand years, they bound her soul with red ropes so that she would grow up safe and unable to harm anyone.

One day at the Lantern Rite Moon Carver, together with Rex Lapis and Mountain Shaper, borrowed the mechanism to cook food from Cloud Retainer and spent the evening making food. Despite using their friend's invention, Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver don't understand Cloud Retainer's love towards the mechanisms and haute cuisine.
One day, Moon Carver imagined he could outrun Cloud Retainer on her "Bi-Cyclical Thunderflash-Mobile,” which she had spent forty-nine days developing. He ran with all his might, but was outpaced by the mechanism's speed. The only drawback was its inability to navigate mountainous terrain, and it went off the track. Another time, it snowed heavily in Liyue, and Mt. Aocang was covered in several feet of snow. Cloud Retainer created a Snowdrift Mechanism for skiing on the mountains. Together with Guizhong and Streetward Rambler, she had a tremendous time until Moon Carver decided to join in. Moments later, he had managed to send the mechanism flying off the rails and plummeted deep into a snowbank. It took the Adepti hours to dig him up. Later, Cloud Retainer added many safety features to the mechanism so that even a three-year-old child could operate it.

Nowadays, Moon Carver often walks on Mt. Tianheng and enjoys the city's views. According to Cloud Retainer, he really wanted to see how it was going in Liyue, but because of the contract with the Liyue Qixing, he couldn't visit Liyue and manage the work as he pleased. However, Madame Ping's old friends, including Moon Carver, quite often visit her in the harbor. ​​Guests will often not only visit the stores and food stands but also attend storytelling sessions or Liyue opera performances at Heyu Tea House. Once, three outlanders, first-time visitors to Liyue Harbor, sat at the table beside that of Yaoyao and company. Having heard an opera about the Adepti of Liyue, they began to discuss that very topic over tea and snacks. Unable to get a word in lengthwise in the conversation between her master and her guest, Yaoyao succumbed to boredom, listening in on the nearby chat while eating some treats. The adventurer from Mondstadt asked the tea master if they had ever spoken to an Adeptus, only to be disappointed by the reply: <color=#ffffffd9>"It is but a story, for we mortals do not daily dwell in Jueyun Karst, and few are the opportunities to meet the Adepti."</color> Yaoyao, finding this statement to be incorrect, could not help but rebut thusly: <color=#ece5d8>"</color> <color=#ffffffd9>That's not true. The Adepti are among us. I mean, Uncle Moon Carver just said that the story was very interesting."</color>

customize.text: Vibrant Harriers Aloft in Spring Breeze

Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver visited Liyue Harbor during the Lantern Rite to meet with Cloud Retainer. They disguised themselves as mortals, Houzhang and Jiehu, so that people would not recognize them. The Traveler and Paimon initially mistook the Adepti for Treasure Hoarders, and they had to prove they were illuminated beasts.
During Cloud Retainer's kite-flying master class on Mt. Aocang, the Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper were flying a kite on a nearby mountain. The kite accidentally ended up on Mt. Aocang, and they had to meet Cloud Retainer, who immediately recognized them as old friends. Later, the Adepti participated in Cloud Retainer's plan to help a young man from Chenyu Vale, Gaming, reunite with his father. They pretended to be the Treasure Hoarders and distracted Gaming while the Traveler and Paimon followed the plan and took Gaming's father away.

At the Lantern Rite, which honored the memory of the deceased Yaksha, Menogias, Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver recalled that as a master of handicrafts, it would not have been difficult for Menogias to create kites. If he was still alive, he could have opened his own kite shop, which would have brought him not only great profit but also even greater respect. And if Menogias, as before, did not dare to get involved in human affairs, he could have entrusted the sale of kites to them. Thus, while thinking about how they would celebrate their success together in wonderful company with a bottle of wine, the Adepti were filled with happy memories and enjoyed the beauty of the harbor beyond Menogias.

customize.text: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon

Shortly before the Lantern Rite, dedicated to the White Horse Adeptus, people saw an unusual phenomenon in the sky: the moon was obscured by a black shadow, as if a piece had been bitten off. This phenomenon was caused by the real moon appearing in the sky of Teyvat, and the projection of the moon, which had hung there for six thousand years, began to disappear. When this process occurred, people saw the moon being obscured by a black shadow. And when it stopped, the black shadow disappeared, becoming invisible to the naked eye. The false moon held a fragment of the White Horse Adeptus's soul, and if the false moon disintegrated, the soul would disappear with it. Rex Lapis decided to take advantage of this moment to rescue the White Horse Adeptus. To do so, he, the Traveler, and Paimon set out to find the other two soul fragments of the Lord of Geo's old friend. Furthermore, Morax instructed all the Adepti to keep a close watch on Liyue Harbor. He didn't want to endanger them by recounting the events of ancient times, so he didn't explain the situation.

When Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper were ordered to rush to Liyue Harbor to keep watch, Mountain Shaper decided to tend to the mint he and Moon Carver had planted. When the mint became infected with diseases and parasites, Moon Carver transplanted them to Mt. Hulao, but Cloud Retainer didn't appreciate such compassion for the plants and angrily banished both Adepti to the desert. When they finally returned to the harbor, they saw their old acquaintance, Gaming, and the Treasure Hoarders. It turned out that it wasn't Gaming who was in danger, but the Treasure Hoarders themselves. Gaming was pursuing them to become his disciples in the Wushou Dance, and he wouldn't take no for an answer. Upon closer inspection, the Adepti noticed the boy was possessed. The Traveler and Paimon came to their aid, going after Gaming, knowing that he had been possessed by one of the White Horse Adeptus’s Deadly Selves. Provoked, the Deadly Self was forced to leave the dancer's body and possess Mountain Shaper. Under the influence of the possession, the Adeptus decided to fulfill his greatest desire: to sow mint in Cloud Retainer's abode to anger her. When the Deadly Self left Gaming's body, he fainted from exhaustion, and Moon Carver, in mortal form, accompanied him to Liyue Harbor. Since he was equal in power to Mountain Shaper, the Adeptus knew that if he pursued the Deadly Self, it would migrate into him.

While Mountain Shaper was planting the mint, Moon Carver, Cloud Retainer, Conqueror of Demons, and Streetward Rambler devised a plan to lure out the White Horse Adeptus's Deadly Self. They decided to seal off the exits from Mt. Aocang, and the Traveler would be the only one into whom the Deadly Self could possess. But due to their strength, they would be able to resist this and speak with the White Horse Adeptus. When, upon meeting the Traveler, the Deadly Self agreed to surrender the fragment of the White Horse Adeptus's soul contained within her, Mountain Shaper awoke from his possession.

customize.text: Character Story

<color=#ffd780>Character Story 3</color>
Once, three outlanders, first-time visitors to Liyue Harbor, sat at the table beside that of Yaoyao and company. Having heard an opera about the adepti of Liyue, they began to discuss that very topic over tea and snacks.
The adventurer from Mondstadt was for his part very taken with the legends of the adepti, for he had only heard the bards sing songs of the gods, but had never himself met one or any of their familiars.
Unable to resist, he asked the tea master if they had ever spoken to an adeptus, only to be disappointed by the reply:
"It is but a story, for we mortals do not daily dwell in Jueyun Karst, and few are the opportunities to meet the adepti."
Yaoyao, finding this statement to be incorrect, could not help but rebut thusly: "That's not true. The adepti are among us. I mean, Uncle Moon Carver just said that the story was very interesting."
For some reason she could not fathom, Madame Ping's guest stopped speaking altogether, and Madame Ping laughed, saying a few words to the tea master to change the topic.
Yaoyao, however, did not understand: Why did people find the adepti very distant from their daily lives? The adepti were amongst them — they just didn't readily reveal themselves, that's all.

customize.text: Character Story

<color=#ffd780>Character Story 5</color>
Liyue has its own fortune-telling, destiny-reading methods, similar to astrology.
Of these, there are two fates that people seek to avoid at all costs.
One is that of the "solitary star," which dictates that one will be separated from friends and family, living alone all one's days.
The other is "disastrous evil," which means that one will face many hardships and perils.
When the adepti rescued Shenhe, Moon Carver did once read her fortune.
The signs showed that she was marked by both the "solitary star" and "disastrous evil," and that she was also plagued by intense homicidal urges — she was thus a person of supremely ominous destiny, doomed to harm both herself and others.
To ensure that she could grow up safely and not harm any innocents, the adepti bound her soul using red ropes.
This binding had the effect of restraining both her evil fate and her violent tendencies, but also shackled many emotions that should have originally belonged to a human.
From then on, she became more and more disaffected by trivial matters, and even things most might consider important were but dust to her.
She became ever less human, and ever more like a lovely yet cold statue.
But surprisingly, she felt something stir within her when she encountered that Traveler from a distant land:
Long-dormant emotions, now strangers to her, came loose all at once from the depths of fate's tableau.
Perhaps it really was as Moon Carver once said: that heaven might dictate fates, but destiny's tale is written by mortals. The tale of Shenhe and the mortal world had not yet ended...
<color=#ffd780>Vision</color>
Few people know how the young girl in the cave, intended as a sacrifice by her own father, had been able to stand against the monster for days and nights on end by herself.
Though Shenhe was born into an exorcist family, her maddened father had not taught her a single thing about exorcism.
And like many at that innocent age, she was also wholly unused to facing life's perils alone.
But in that aphotic cave, bereft of parental protection — indeed, betrayed by kin — Shenhe underwent a metamorphosis.
Just as Moon Carver's readings had shown, the sleeping calamitous fates, violent urges, and unyielding spirit within her burst their bonds all at once.
Those things served as an unseen shield and invisible blade, arming the girl's frail form.
They gave her strength, gave her claws and fangs, allowing her to attack that wretched creature before her, to swear to tear it to shreds — to prove that she, and not it, was the cruelest evil that stalked the darkness.
Their life-and-death battle across the next few days was one without end. Hunter and hunted switched places many times, the conflict locked in stalemate...
As the shadow of death loomed large, the gods looked upon the extraordinary girl with favor.
With the bright, crystalline object falling into Shenhe's hands, the balance tipped irrevocably in her favor and the victor was decided.
The vivid icy light pierced through the dark like skyglow, showing the path to the future.
In the past, it had guided Shenhe from her miserable fate. In the future, it would also lead her back to the mortal realm.

customize.text: Character Story

<color=#ffd780>Character Details</color>
As for where the adepti dwell, the "Full Record of Pristine Pavilion" asserts that the sky is their pillow and the earth their mat, and that they may dwell in the mountains, rivers, lakes, and seas — and this indeed seems to explain the countless adeptal encounters recorded in the annals of Liyue's history. This is one school of thought.
Another can be found in the classic treatise on metal and stone, "Void-Pacing Stone Catalog." While showering praise upon the weird and wonderful rock formations of Jueyun Karst, "Stone Catalog" also proffers a warning: "The peaks of Jueyun tower up to lofty heights, striving to outdo one another... each belonging to a different master — Qingyun Peak to Moon Carver, Mt. Hulao to Mountain Shaper, Mt. Aocang to Cloud Retainer. The wise climb not a mastered mountain, nor quarry its rocks."
<color=#ffd780>Character Story 1</color>
Every second of every day, Liyue Harbor bustles with throngs of people coming and going. Local businessman weighed down by sacks of gold, outlanders garbed in strange attire, shrewd and canny public servants, warm-hearted guards... People from all walks of life with all sorts of personalities mingle, to the extent that no one looks out of place.
When someone new suddenly appears in a city like this, people don't bat an eyelid.
This particular newcomer to Liyue Harbor is a woman who goes by the name of Xianyun. Tall and slender, she wears a pair of red-rimmed spectacles and exudes an aura that makes her stand out from the crowd.
To the Fontainian merchants who sell their mechanical creations on the streets of Liyue, she's already a familiar figure. When passing by, she invariably stops to discuss mechanical design with them — and once such discussions get started, entire afternoons fly by before anyone notices. She seems well acquainted with Chef Mao and Xiangling from Wanmin Restaurant as well, and is often to be seen sitting at a table opposite Guoba, waiting for a bowl of piping hot Dragon Beard Noodles. And she's also made an impression on the waiters of both Xinyue Kiosk and Liuli Pavilion, where she sometimes dines as the guest of Mr. Zhongli from the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. Granny Shan, the toy seller, remembers her too. If memory serves, she'd tell you, Xianyun's the one who often brings along a young woman with long, white hair to look at her kites and other trinkets. The young woman, whose name she now recalls is Shenhe, never seems to find anything that takes her fancy — yet Xianyun always brings her back nonetheless.
Just like many other residents of Liyue Harbor, it seems that Xianyun not only has hobbies of her own, but also travels widely and has many friends.
So when people see her chatting with Madame Ping by the fish pond nearby Yujing Terrace, they think nothing of it.
"I haven't seen much of Mountain Shaper lately. And Moon Carver still hasn't returned that Multi-Purpose Abode Cleaning Talisman I lent him, to this day..."
"Is that so? What might that be then, some sort of new sigil contraption you've come up with?"
"Yes, let me tell you all about it..."
<color=#ffd780>Jadevoid</color>
Legend has it that the place where an adeptus resides is known as their Jadevoid. The adeptal abodes tucked away among the peaks of Jueyun Karst are just such places.
The word "Jadevoid" originates from a spot among the clouds high above Qingyun Peak which overlooks the world below. This is a place that has rarely been seen by mortal eyes.
"Jade" refers to the foundation of this place, which was made from a single piece of Plaustrite — hence why it floats above the clouds.
The true way is found in emptiness, and thus can be attained by traversing the void. Once, those who sought the path of the adepti had to pass the trials of heaven and earth. This place served as the trial of "heaven."
Originally, however, the Jadevoid was not created by the adepti as a test of the spirit. Instead, it was created by Cloud Retainer as a locale for reflection and meditation. It was only later that Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper persuaded her to lend this place for the benefit of those who might come seeking the adeptal path. Hearing that Rex Lapis had given his assent and that Guizhong and Streetward Rambler both agreed as well, Cloud Retainer readily gave up the Jadevoid and had a small pavilion built upon it.
Nowadays, few are able to follow the adeptal path, and the Jadevoid — almost nothing now but a legend among mortals — has returned to the care of Cloud Retainer. But today, returning to this place above the clouds, her state of mind has changed.
Though the vast sea of clouds and the sight of the sun as it rises and sets are as magnificent as ever, her thoughts have begun to drift off to the lively bustle of the mortal world.
Now, she yearns to live alongside the humans under the name of Xianyun.
"As it just so happens, I'm starting to feel hungry. How about... some of Wanmin Restaurant's delectable Crab Roe Tofu."
Voice-Over

<color=#ffd780>More about Xianyun: IV</color>
For all the wondrous feats that can be accomplished by one who has mastered the mechanical arts, one often uses it for purely recreational purposes. There was one year when it snowed heavily in Liyue, and Mt. Aocang was covered in several feet of snow. Seeing everyone cooped up in their abodes with nothing to do, one created a Snowdrift Mechanism for skiing on the mountains. One was having a tremendous time of it along with Guizhong and Streetward Rambler... until, of course, Moon Carver noticed as much and decided to join in. Moments later, he had managed to send the mechanism flying off the rails and plummeted deep into a snow bank. It took us hours to dig him out... Later, one introduced a great many safety features to the mechanism, to the point where it could be safely piloted by even a three-year-old child. Although this did entail a compromise on the top speed of the vehicle.
